name: Voter register and Permanent Voter Card (PVC) collection statistics
geographicCoverage: National, state, LGA, registration area and polling-unit level depending on the specific release
dataType: Administrative voter-registration totals and certified PVC collection tables (PDF / web publications)
updateFrequency: Election-cycle and event-based; specific publication dates and reference cutoffs must be retained
licence: No blanket reuse licence confirmed; cite the exact INEC publication and check applicable terms.
checkedHow: INEC official PVC statistics page, 13 August 2026 Osun release, 2025–2026 CVR closure notice, February 2026 Chairman remarks and 2023 nationwide PVC summary reviewed.
limitations: Registered voters, newly registered CVR applicants, PVCs printed, PVCs distributed, PVCs collected and accredited voters are different measures and must not be combined.
The nationwide 2023 collection snapshot is dated 5 February 2023; it is not a current 2026 PVC collection total.
INEC's 2026 Osun release reports 1,518,485 collected PVCs for that election across 30 LGAs; it is a state election snapshot, not a nationwide total.
Polling-unit and LGA coverage depends on the particular certified file; do not infer missing rows as zero.
The official 2023 report and briefing should be used to reconcile denominators and state totals before calculating derived rates.

A programmatic reconciliation of the official 2023 PDF found that 16 state-level uncollected-PVC values do not equal registered voters minus collected PVCs; the state-row sum of published uncollected counts (6,259,231) also differs from INEC's printed national total (6,259,229), while the arithmetic difference is 6,260,001. The register and collected-PVC state rows do sum to their national totals.

INEC's CVR portal currently states that registration has ended and administrative processing of applications is ongoing. This is not the final validated register; a consolidated national and state/LGA post-CVR total has not been located.
notes: 2023 nationwide snapshot: 93,469,008 registered voters; 87,209,007 PVCs collected as at 5 February 2023 (93.3% reported by INEC). Kaduna: 4,335,208 registered; 4,164,473 collected (96.1%). These are historical figures, not a current register. A structured 37-geography transcription is stored in data/indicators/inec-pvc-2023.json with both reported and calculated values kept separate. INEC's 2026 Osun off-cycle release reports 1,518,485 collected PVCs across 30 LGAs with a certified polling-unit-level breakdown. This is an Osun election snapshot, not a national total. Current status: https://cvr.inecnigeria.org/Home/cvrEnded. The portal closure notice is a process-status update, not a final count. INEC's 13 August 2026 Osun PVC release reports 1,518,485 collected PVCs across 30 LGAs.

name: Continuous Voter Registration (CVR), 2025–2026
geographicCoverage: National; phase totals are currently documented in national statements; state/LGA disaggregation requires a separate official table
dataType: Administrative registration activity statements and press releases
updateFrequency: Phase-based; final consolidated post-exercise release required
licence: Cite INEC's exact statement; no blanket reuse licence confirmed.
checkedHow: INEC Chairman's 4–5 February 2026 official remarks and INEC press release describing phase one and the scheduled exercise period reviewed.
limitations: INEC reported 2,782,587 new eligible voters in phase one (18 August–10 December 2025) in the Chairman's remarks; a separate INEC press release reported 2,782,589. Preserve this two-person discrepancy until the Commission clarifies the authoritative total.

The February 2026 statement described phase two as 5 January–17 April 2026 and the full exercise as scheduled to conclude 30 August 2026; this is a schedule, not evidence that the exercise concluded or the final total.
As at this review, no final consolidated nationwide CVR result after the scheduled August 2026 conclusion was located.
CVR registrations are not the same as the validated final voter register or collected PVCs; duplicate and ineligible records may be removed during validation.

INEC's published CVR timetable lists phase three registration from 4 May to 17 August 2026 and display for claims/objections from 24 to 30 August 2026. This confirms the planned timetable, not the final validated nationwide register.

INEC's 9 June 2026 bulletin reports an Ekiti election register of 1,059,360, comprising a 2023 base of 987,647 plus 66,664 new registrants. These components sum to 1,054,311, leaving 5,049 voters unexplained in the bulletin; do not infer the reason without a reconciliation from INEC.
notes: Do not publish a single 'current registered voters' number by adding phase one CVR to the 2023 register. Obtain INEC's final post-CVR register and state/LGA tables, with validation date and treatment of transfers, duplicates and deceased registrants. A 9 June 2026 INEC bulletin gives an Ekiti-specific register of 1,059,360, 66,664 new registrants against a 2023 base of 987,647, and 2,103 double registrations invalidated; the arithmetic components do not reconcile and are stored as separate reported facts. No final national post-CVR total has been located.

The exercise is described as a census of public and private basic education schools, but coverage and response quality should be checked in the report's methodology and tables.
School-level GPS capture does not guarantee that a public machine-readable school register is available.
Enrolment counts do not equal unique children in the population; school attendance, enrolment, completion and learning outcomes are different measures.
State-level comparisons require consistent definitions, private/public coverage and reporting completeness.
notes: UBEC's reports index also lists a 2024 Annual Report and a 4th Quarter 2025 Key Performance Report. These are separate publications and should be assessed independently before integration.
